headline: Meta Q3 revenue up 26% to $64.6B, Q4 guide $73-76B; shares up after hours
summary: GAAP EPS was $3.83 after a $9.9B charge for the state attorneys general settlement ($7.40 excluding it). 2026 capex is now $135-145B (was $130-145B), with no 2027 figure given yet; shares rose 3-5% after hours.

headline: Meta to issue non-voting Class C shares as a one-for-one stock dividend
summary: Effective January 2027, each Class A and B share gets one Class C share, which works like a two-for-one split with no change to voting control. Q3 capex of $34.9B exceeded operating cash flow, and Meta expects Reality Labs losses near $15B next year.

headline: Huang at GTC Berlin: every European company will become an AI company
summary: Nvidia showed a factory-built DSX POD data center module on Vera Rubin that can be deployed in about two weeks, and said it has committed nearly $10B to Europe's tech ecosystem. Shares rose 2.5% on the day.

headline: Micron signs labour deal with Taichung union; Taoyuan strike still planned
summary: The Taichung union signed a collective agreement and cancelled the Oct 22 mediation. The Taoyuan union, which wants 15% of operating profit shared with staff, had not called off its one-day warning strike.

headline: Alphabet slips ahead of Oct 28 results; KeyBanc trims target
summary: KeyBanc cut its target to $410 from $435 (still Overweight), and a London Google Cloud data center outage on Oct 20 disrupted UK banks. OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden.

headline: Alibaba falls about 4% as US-listed China tech sells off
summary: No single trigger; coverage cites heavy AI capex weighing on free cash flow, weak Chinese consumer spending and chip export limits.

headline: Tesla Q3: EPS and cash flow beat, revenue a hair light, stock flat to slightly up after hours
summary: Adj. EPS $0.48 vs $0.44 expected, revenue $28.05B vs $28.13B, free cash flow +$1.53B vs an expected $4.9B outflow, and Q3 capex $4.7B. Full-year capex is guided above $25B for Optimus (now in production at Fremont), AI compute, Cybercab and Terafab; shares rose 3.4% in the session and about 0.5% after hours.

headline: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, an always-on agent, as a research preview
summary: Claude Duet runs on its own cloud computer, handling email, calendar and app tasks in the background, and asks before sending, paying or deleting anything. It is rolling out by waitlist to US Pro and Max subscribers at no extra cost.

headline: Robinhood up about 4% after Rosenblatt starts coverage at Buy
summary: Rosenblatt initiated at Buy with a $135 target and called it a "generational growth story", and a bitcoin rebound lifted crypto-linked names. Q3 results are due next week.

headline: BYD falls about 3% as September China retail drops 29% and CATL disappoints
summary: BYD's domestic passenger retail sales were 246,816 in September (down 28.9% y/y), though it still led with a 22.8% NEV share and overseas sales are booming. Q3 results are due Oct 29.

headline: Lam Research down 6% after hours despite a beat, while TXN guides Q4 above estimates
summary: Lam posted revenue of $8.22B vs $8.13B and guided December to $8.6B +/- $0.4B (consensus $8.54B), but the wide range and an 80% one-year run prompted selling. Texas Instruments revenue rose 28% to $6.06B and it guided Q4 EPS to $2.45-2.79 vs $2.27 expected.

headline: Brent touched $112 on Iranian mine claims in Hormuz, then settled near $109
summary: The IRGC claimed mines stopped three tankers on a route it calls unauthorized, and the US disputes the claims. Prices eased after Iran said indirect talks with Washington continue; Brent settled at $108.79 Tuesday and $108.82 Wednesday.

headline: BofA previews 44% Q3 order growth; GE Vernova up 4%
summary: BofA reaffirmed Buy ($1,310) ahead of the Oct 28 report, forecasting about 44% y/y order growth. GE Vernova also won a 9E turbine order for a 372 MW plant in Cote d'Ivoire.

headline: Netflix beats on Q3 EPS but cuts 2026 ad revenue forecast to $2.7B
summary: Q3 revenue was $12.9B (+12%) and EPS $0.87 against $0.82 expected. 2026 revenue guidance is $51.1B, slightly below the prior midpoint, and Q4 margin guidance includes the cost of headcount cuts.

headline: Netflix falls about 6% after hours as ads lag and layoffs are announced
summary: Management said the ads business is behind target because of delayed product rollouts, though ad revenue is still growing over 80%. Full 2027 guidance comes in January.

headline: Micron Taoyuan union calls one-day solidarity strike for Oct 22
summary: The union represents about 2,400 of roughly 3,000 Taoyuan workers; it has not said how many will walk out, and no production impact has been reported.

headline: Tesla and SpaceX boards form special committees to review a merger
summary: On SpaceX's Q3 call, Musk said independent-director committees at both companies are evaluating a combination, with no terms agreed. Tesla would need approval from a majority of all outstanding shares, which Musk called a high hurdle.

headline: Anthropic draft prospectus (per WSJ): Q3 revenue $16.8B, up 45% q/q; H1 net loss $80.7B
summary: WSJ-reported figures from a leaked draft S-1 show H1 revenue of $16.3B, two customers at about a fifth of sales, and cloud spend that could top $750B. The loss is not broken down; a November IPO is reportedly still the target.

headline: Cursor added $608M of revenue in its first 7 weeks inside SpaceX
summary: SpaceX's Q3 report showed Cursor contributing $608M from its Aug 14 close to Sep 30, inside an AI segment whose revenue rose to $7.56B. Cursor is now a SpaceX subsidiary, so it has no standalone funding rounds.

headline: Cloudflare patches products after eMudhra certificate keys were compromised
summary: Private keys for 8 widely trusted eMudhra intermediate certificates were exposed. Cloudflare deployed fixes within about 26 hours, found no exploitation on its services, and told customers to update WARP and cloudflared (2026.10.2) and review mTLS trust stores.

headline: 10-year at 5.14%; October hike odds about 17%, December about 90%
summary: Odds of an October hike fell from about 50% after Chair Warsh declined to signal a move this month, but markets still expect one by December. The FOMC meets Oct 27-28, with the decision at Thu Oct 29 05:00 AEDT.

headline: Sea launches enterprise cloud arm, weighs Monee IPO
summary: A CEO memo filed Oct 20 said Sea will sell AI cloud services to businesses (Sea Cloud) and is considering listing its Monee fintech arm. No capex, timing or valuation given. Shares fell 16.9% over Oct 19-21 to $77.94.

headline: Amazon up 5% as Morgan Stanley names it a top pick
summary: Morgan Stanley raised its target to $350 from $335 and sees AWS operating margins reaching 42% in 2027. Q3 results are due Oct 29 after the US close.

headline: OpenAI still in talks on ~$30B raise at over $1.4T
summary: Reuters reported the talks are ongoing, so nothing has closed; the last closed round was $852B in March.

headline: Jefferies: iPhone 18 Pro demand weakening, with about 2M units of assembly orders cut
summary: China lead times for the Pro and Pro Max are at zero, PDD cut prices 6-9% on Oct 16, and chip orders were trimmed 10-15%. China sell-through growth slowed from over 40% to about 8%, while the foldable Duo's lead time is over 90 days.

headline: Chip index snaps its 8-day losing streak, its longest since 2008
summary: The SOX rose about 2.7% on Oct 19 after losing about 15.7% over eight sessions, led by memory names. The Nasdaq added 1.1% on Oct 21.

headline: China Q3 GDP grows 4.5%, ahead of the 4.4% forecast
summary: GDP rose 1.2% q/q, September industrial output rose 5.5% and retail sales 1.1%, while fixed asset investment fell 7.2% year to date. Exports are carrying growth and the property market is still weak.

headline: JPMorgan: big cloud firms spending about 93% of operating cash flow on AI
summary: Weekend piece notes hyperscaler AI capex at about 93% of operating cash flow, up from 33% in 2023. Alphabet spent more cash than it took in last quarter, a first since its 2004 IPO.

headline: Iran Guards say two tankers hit mines in Hormuz; no independent confirmation
summary: Reuters via IRNA: two tankers carrying about 2m barrels caught fire after hitting mines on an unauthorised route. No confirmation from the US, UKMTO or the owners as of Sunday. Attacks near the strait have risen over two weeks.

headline: CoreWeave ends week down 24% on debt fears
summary: CoreWeave, which rents out Nvidia GPU capacity, fell about 24% for the week. Some of its bond yields neared 15% and its credit default swaps spiked. Evercore ISI and JPMorgan still rate it a buy, citing a backlog of more than $100B.

headline: FT: Anthropic offers Blackstone a coupon above 10% on a $9B slice of $60B TPU debt
summary: Broadcom-arranged $60B package: $42B senior bank loan plus an $18B junior tranche, half of which ($9B) Blackstone funds would take. Coupon above 10% vs about 7% for similar-rated public bonds. It funds part of a $125.2B five-year Google TPU lease, 3.5 GW from 2027. The prospectus flags Broadcom's dual role as supplier and lender, and says some defaults could accelerate lease obligations.

headline: iPhone Duo US delivery dates slip to late January within 30 minutes of pre-orders
summary: Pre-orders opened Fri Oct 16; US estimates reached late January 2027, about three months out, ahead of the Oct 23 in-store launch. Same recap: HomePod mini 2 ($149) ships Oct 30, Apple TV 4K and HomeView ($299 each) ship Nov 13, and Bloomberg reports a media event on Oct 28 for OLED touchscreen MacBook Pros and M6 Macs.

headline: Alibaba rises 2.3% in Hong Kong as Hang Seng Tech gains 1.16%
summary: The Hang Seng closed up 0.52% at 24,186 on HK$178.2 billion turnover, led by tech. Kuaishou rose 2.5% after releasing Kling 4.0 and Lenovo rebounded 8%. Alibaba's US ADR later fell 1.8% in the US tech selloff.

headline: Nasdaq falls 2.1% to 26,140, its worst week since June, on AI-debt worries; CoreWeave -12%
summary: Friday Oct 16: Nasdaq -573 points (-2.1%) to 26,140, S&P 500 -1.1%, Dow -0.3%. CoreWeave fell nearly 12% (about -24% on the week) on debt worries; AMD -6%, Intel -5.8%, Micron -5.6%, Broadcom -4.5%, Tesla -2.1%. CBS also cited doubts over Anthropic's revenue momentum. 10-year yield about 5.1%; CME odds of a December Fed hike 74.3%, up from 50.2% a month ago. Watchlist on the week: CRDO -21.6%, BE -21.1%, TER -19.3%, SKHY ADR -19.3%, NET -17.9%, ALAB -16.5%, CLS -16.1%.

headline: iPhone Duo preorders open at $1,999 and sell out; new orders now ship late January
summary: Apple's first foldable opened for preorder Oct 16 from $1,999 (over $3,000 at 2TB). Within 30 minutes shipping estimates for new orders slipped to late January 2027, more than three months out; 9to5Mac says supply, not demand, is the constraint. Apple rose 0.43% Friday to $343.46 against a 2.1% Nasdaq fall, +2.0% on the week. FQ4 results Nov 2; Duo sales land in the December quarter.

headline: BYD picks Sime Darby's Inokom plant for CKD assembly in Malaysia; HK shares +1.1%
summary: BYD will use existing capacity at Inokom for local assembly in Malaysia; models and timing not announced. BYD had 21.09% of China's EV battery installs in September vs CATL 40.92%. Hong Kong closed Friday at HK$73.75 (+1.10%), -2.4% on the week. Second-gen Seagull launches Oct 20, 19:00 Beijing (22:00 AEDT). Weekly China registrations for October still not published by CnEVPost.

headline: CoreWeave falls more than 11%, nearly 25% on the week; 2031 bond yield briefly topped 16%
summary: Reuters: CoreWeave's October 2031 bond was set for a fifth weekly fall, down about 3 cents this week, and its CDS passed 1,000bp to a record (S&P Global). Nebius, Applied Digital and IREN fell about 11-12% Friday. ARK bought more than 381,000 shares over two sessions.

headline: Chip index falls 3.83%, an eighth straight loss and longest streak since 2008; 23.9% below June record
summary: SOX closed at 11,137.29, down 15.7% since Oct 6. Over that span Nvidia -10.5%, Micron -15.9%, Lam -21.0%, Intel -20.1%; TSMC's ADR fell 2.3% Friday. Yields fell over the period, so rates do not explain it; AI-financing worries are the best-fit reason.

headline: Brent touches $110, first time since May, and settles at $109.86 (+3.7%) on Hormuz attacks and Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
summary: WTI settled at $101.41 (+3.5%). On the week WTI rose more than 10% and Brent nearly 5%. Ukraine also vowed to keep hitting Russian refineries.

headline: US September industrial production rises 0.7% (0.4% expected); import prices +1.1% with fuel +4.8%
summary: Utilities output +3.5%, manufacturing +0.3%, capacity use 76.9%; IP +2.2% y/y. Import prices +8.1% y/y, fuel +34.5% y/y; export prices +2.2% m/m.

headline: Taiwan shares close up 0.3% at 47,111.26 Friday after Thursday's 3.41% drop
summary: The Taiex gained 141.39 points on turnover of NT$935.96 billion. TSMC's Taipei shares slipped 0.8% on the first full session after its results.

headline: Reuters: CoreWeave 2031 bonds yield 15.78%; Oracle, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta CDS at records
summary: CoreWeave carries more than $50B of debt. Oracle, Nvidia and other big-tech credit default swaps rose this week; Amazon, Alphabet and Meta hit records but moved far less than CoreWeave or Oracle. Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid said AI financing costs show worrying signs at the edges.

headline: KOSPI +2.05% after Black Thursday; Samsung +2.6%, SK hynix +0.8%; Nikkei +1.4%
summary: Foreigners bought a net 172.1B won, ending an eight-session selling streak, after selling more than 3.6T won on Thursday. SK hynix faded from about +2.9% intraday. KOSPI is still 19.2% below its Oct 2 close; analysts called the buying a pause, not a reversal.

headline: Warsh gives no October signal in Bangkok: 'will make judgements at the October and December meeting'
summary: In his last appearance before the blackout, the Fed Chair said he does not pre-judge meetings and called the investment surge the main upside for the global economy. The dollar index slipped 0.2%.

headline: Asia rebounds after the chip rout: Nikkei +1.9%, Hang Seng +1.2%; Jakarta falls over 10% on MSCI warning
summary: After Thursday's US close (Dow +1.1%, S&P +0.3%, Nasdaq +0.1%), the Nikkei rose 1.9%, Hang Seng 1.2%, Shanghai 1% and the ASX 200 1.1%. Indonesia slumped on an MSCI downgrade warning; Brent eased 0.4% to about $105.5 (AP).

headline: Netflix names Peter Rice chief content officer from Oct 26; Bela Bajaria leaves
summary: Rice, former chairman of Walt Disney Television and president of 21st Century Fox, will run global series, film and live content. Bajaria leaves after nearly ten years. The change follows the confirmed 6% job cuts and comes days before Q3 results on Wed Oct 21 07:00 AEDT.

headline: Taiwan's president urges Micron and unions to negotiate; COO says Taichung 2027 capacity sold out
summary: Lai Ching-te spoke at the opening of Micron's new Taichung assembly and test plant. Unions want a concrete profit-sharing plan and are urging members to take Oct 19 off for a Taipei rally, which they say is not a strike. COO Manish Bhatia said the plant's 2027 capacity is sold out and HBM should outgrow the rest of DRAM through 2028. Micron has about 15,000 staff in Taiwan.

headline: Reuters: some Anthropic investors now discuss a ~$1.5T IPO valuation, down from ~$2T
summary: Per four people familiar, attendees at Anthropic's investor day in San Francisco (with CEO Dario Amodei and CFO Krishna Rao) discussed about $1.5T for the November IPO after Q3 revenue growth slowed to 45% q/q ($16.8B) from more than doubling in Q2 ($11.6B). Anthropic has committed to at least $518B of cloud and compute spending over a decade. No exchange or banks named; Anthropic did not comment. Cited by CBS as one reason for Friday's tech selloff.

headline: Tesla shows a 'flying' Roadster at SpaceX's Texas site; production 2028; stock reverses to -2.1%
summary: Unveiled Thursday evening at SpaceX's McGregor test facility: compressed-air thrusters for short-burst flight over cars, claimed 0-60 mph in 0.81 s, target top speed Mach 0.5, no price given. Musk said production starts 2028. Friday the stock opened $369.15, hit $385.51, then closed -2.13% at $354.72 in the tech selloff. Q3 results Oct 21 after close (08:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22).

headline: TSMC raises 2026 sales growth forecast to about 44% in US dollars, keeps capex at $60-64B
summary: Up from slightly over 40% in July. CFO Wendell Huang kept 2026 capex at $60-64 billion and said 2026-2028 spending will exceed the prior three years. 2nm was 8% of Q3 sales, up from 3% in Q2. CoWoS remains customers' top choice and TSMC will add capacity to meet demand.

headline: TSMC call: AI accelerator growth 'probably will be higher' than mid-to-high 50s%; 'prudent' on 2027
summary: Management did not formally lift the 2024-2029 AI accelerator CAGR but said it will probably be higher. Consumer and price-sensitive segments are being challenged by rising component prices. Overseas-fab margin dilution to widen to 3-4 points later in the five-year period. N2 capacity to more than double in 2027; A14 risk production 2027.

headline: TSMC weighing Texas production and cooperation with Musk's Terafab; Arizona second fab in Q3 2027
summary: C.C. Wei said talks are at the discussion stage and TSMC would need to run any fab it works on. He said US expansion is driven by requests from major American customers. Arizona's second fab is slated for volume production in Q3 2027.

headline: Huang says CoreWeave needs no backstop as its credit swaps hit a record 1,194.5bp
summary: Speaking in Stockholm, Huang said CoreWeave's cost of capital is decreasing. The CDS level implies over 60% default odds within five years. Nvidia owns about 10% of CoreWeave. Separately reported, unconfirmed: talks to backstop $250 billion of OpenAI data-centre financing.

headline: Nvidia and Volvo Cars expand partnership on automated driving safety
summary: One of two Nvidia partnership releases Thursday; the other expands work with Adobe on agentic creation tools.

headline: Meta launches Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter open-weight model that runs on Mac Studio
summary: Natively multimodal with a 1 million-token context window, aimed at coding and agentic work; Meta calls it the most capable US open-weight model. Built with Apple to run locally; needs about 1TB of RAM. Available now through several API platforms.

headline: Tim Cook: Apple Intelligence with Alibaba's Qwen approved in China; beta due later in October
summary: Speaking in Shanghai, Cook said the first batch of core features can now be rolled out gradually: live translation, writing tools and photo cleanup. The upgraded Siri is not included.

headline: Anthropic gives six METR researchers employee-level access to assess its models and safety work
summary: METR gets company laptops and internal tools and will publish its own assessments; Anthropic can require redactions only in pre-set categories such as customer data. No IPO, S-1 or revenue update came with it.

headline: US PPI jumps 1.3% in September, most in 4-1/2 years; retail sales +0.8% but core sales only +0.1%
summary: Producer prices rose 1.3% (0.5% expected) and 6.3% y/y on energy; retail sales beat at +0.8% (0.3% expected) but the control group rose just 0.1% vs 0.3%. Claims 199K. Reuters cited about 30% odds of an Oct 28 hike, with December the expected move; yields slipped.

headline: Fed's Hammack: inflation-expectation slippage could force a bigger response
summary: The Cleveland Fed president, a voter and early hike supporter, said the Fed 'might need to move even more' if an inflationary mindset sets in and that financial conditions are roughly neutral; no firm call on October (Reuters).

headline: WTI rises 2.8% on an 8.5M-barrel US crude draw; Trump weighs easing shadow-fleet tanker sanctions
summary: Largest weekly crude draw since February; total US stocks including the SPR are the lowest since March 1984. Brent held near $105.8 as Hormuz and Houthi-Saudi risks offset IEA stock releases.

headline: TSMC Q3 beats: revenue $46.72B (+41.2% y/y) vs $44.6-45.8B guide, gross margin 66.4%, EPS NT$29.43 (+68.7%)
summary: Net income NT$763.06B. Gross margin 66.4% sat inside the 65-67% guide, down from 67.7% in Q2 on early 2nm costs; operating margin 58.7%. 2nm was 8% of wafer revenue (3% in Q2), 3nm 33%. HPC rose to 68% of revenue from 66% in Q2 and 57% a year ago. Q3 capex NT$443.2B. EPS is US$4.60 per ADR.

headline: TSMC guides Q4 revenue to $52.3-54.3B, about 14% above Q3 at the midpoint, with 65-67% gross margin
summary: Operating margin guided to 56.5-58.5% at 31.8 NT$ per US$. CFO Wendell Huang cited continued strong leading-edge demand and the steep 2nm ramp. Good read for Nvidia and custom-chip suppliers like Marvell; it says nothing directly about memory.

headline: Taiwan shares close down 3.41% at 46,969.87 before TSMC's results
summary: The Taiex fell 1,655.96 points on turnover of NT$1.32 trillion. TSMC closed down 2.0% in Taipei; results came out after the close.

headline: Hong Kong opens lower on US rate-hike bets; Alibaba and Tencent down nearly 2%
summary: Hang Seng -0.8% at the open and the tech index -2.21%; Hua Hong -5.6%, SMIC -3.3%. The Hang Seng closed down 1.4%.

headline: Q3 growth slowdown tempers the $2T pitch; SemiAnalysis sees about $74B run rate at year-end
summary: Q3 growth of about 50% compares with roughly 140% in Q2. Some investors had talked of $100B+ annualised revenue by year-end; SemiAnalysis now projects about $74B (from $65B in July). Pressures cited: Meta and Microsoft using own models, cut distillation revenue (5-7% of sales), price war with OpenAI and Chinese labs. Commitments of at least $518B over a decade; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead the IPO.

headline: TSMC guides Q4 revenue $52.3-54.3B vs about $48.8B expected
summary: Q4 gross margin guide 65-67% (expected 66.1%), operating margin 56.5-58.8% (expected 58.0%). Midpoint implies about 14% sequential growth. Read-through for ASML, Teradyne and the AI-connectivity names: accelerator volumes still rising into year-end.

headline: KOSPI hits circuit breaker; SK hynix falls 11% and Samsung 10% in Seoul
summary: Kospi was down 8.13% at 13:17 KST after a sell-sidecar at 09:07 and a 20-minute circuit breaker at 12:38; Kosdaq also halted. SK hynix closed at 1,262,000 won (-11.06%), market cap below 1,000 trillion won. Follows Wall Street's CPI-driven tech selloff and the week's CXMT DRAM worries; KOSPI on a seven-session losing streak.

headline: KOSPI closes down 7.57% after a circuit breaker; Nikkei -4.9%, Taiex -3.41% in an Asia chip rout
summary: KOSPI 5,554.22, KOSDAQ 760.82; SK hynix and Samsung fell about 10-11%. Nikkei 64,425.95 (SoftBank -9.4%, Kioxia -11.2%); Taiex 46,969.87. Hot US CPI, AI-debt worries (CoreWeave bonds, a Gartner impairment warning) and an IMF warning that an AI correction would hit Asia hardest.

headline: Australia sheds 39,300 jobs in September; unemployment 4.7% vs 4.6% expected
summary: Economists expected a 19,600 gain; August revised to +29,300 and 4.7%. Participation 66.8%. AUD -0.3%. ANZ still expects a November hike; Oxford Economics says the RBA has room to wait for Q3 CPI on Oct 28.

headline: Vertiv sets Q3 results for Wed Oct 28 before the US open, call 11am ET
summary: Announced Oct 14: Q3 2026 results Wed Oct 28 before market open; call 11:00 ET (02:00 AEDT Thu Oct 29), with a Q3 presentation on investors.vertiv.com. Company guide is Q3 sales $3.65-3.85B and EPS $1.77-1.83. Not Oct 21 as previously listed. Stock -3.88% Friday to $206.42, a seventh straight fall.

headline: Nvidia falls 3.2% on CPI, IDC China share data and Microsoft's Maia 300 plan
summary: IDC said Nvidia's share of China's AI data-centre chip market fell to 34% in H1 2026 as Huawei grew. Microsoft plans to deploy over a million Maia 300 chips from 2027. Huang said he would halt supply to a customer building unsafe AI, calling it hypothetical.

headline: Netflix confirms about 6% job cuts, nearly 1,000 roles, its largest since 2022
summary: Co-CEO memo; product, technology, legal and HR most affected. Netflix had about 16,000 full-time staff at end-2025. Q3 results due Oct 20 US (07:00 AEDT Wed Oct 21).

headline: Anthropic tells investors Q3 revenue was $16.8B, adjusted profitable and cash-flow positive
summary: At its San Francisco investor day (FT, via Investing.com): Q3 revenue $16.8B, up nearly 50% from about $11.5B in Q2; second straight quarter of adjusted profit; $1.70 of revenue per $1 of compute. Growth slowed from earlier in 2026 and annualised revenue is expected to fall short of $100B. Unaudited, from people familiar.

headline: Hot US CPI (3.7% vs 3.6%) drives Nasdaq down 1.9%; AI stocks lead losses
summary: September CPI 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected (August 3.4%); core 2.6% vs 2.5%. S&P 500 -1.1%, Nasdaq -1.9%, Dow -0.1%; 10-year yield near 5.2-5.3%. Odds of an October Fed hike rose. Watchlist AI-infrastructure names fell 6-10% (Credo, Celestica, Bloom, Astera, GE Vernova, Vertiv). Bank of America fell about 5% after a $1.2B regulatory penalty.

headline: CoreWeave falls 15.5% as its 2032 bonds drop below 80c and yield near 15%
summary: The 9.625% notes sold at par in June fell below 78c per Bloomberg, a yield of about 14.8%; CDS imply a better-than-50% five-year default probability. Nebius fell 10.1% and Oracle 8.8%.

headline: US September CPI 3.7% y/y and core 2.6%, both above forecasts; gasoline up 34% on the year
summary: Headline +0.6% m/m (3.6% y/y expected, 3.4% in August); core +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected. Energy +5.2% m/m, gasoline +9.1% m/m, over half the monthly rise; shelter +0.4%. Last CPI before the Oct 27-28 FOMC.

headline: Bank of America EPS $0.91 after $1.2B money-laundering fine; Morgan Stanley EPS $3.03 on 41% equities growth
summary: BofA's non-deductible fine cost about 17 cents a share (about $1.08 before it); revenue $29.96B. Morgan Stanley revenue $20.3B, ROTCE 22.6%, record wealth revenue $9.1B. Shares fell 4.8% and about 3%.

headline: Beige Book: oil prices in every district, price growth picking up in four; firms slow hiring after AI investment
summary: Two districts reported moderate growth, three modest, four slight, three flat; manufacturing led. Three districts called price growth robust; firms expect further increases as contracts reset. Five districts said firms cut staff by attrition or delayed hiring after AI productivity gains.

headline: ASML shares fall about 4% in first reaction: sales slightly under the EUR 11.72B consensus, profit well above
summary: XTB: revenue EUR 11.66B vs EUR 11.72B expected; net profit EUR 4.96B vs about EUR 4.1B; gross margin 57.5% vs about 56.1%. Amsterdam had already closed down 4.2% Tuesday at EUR 1,509.60.

headline: ASML Q3 sales EUR 11.66B, a hair under consensus; says 2027-28 supply will not meet AI demand
summary: Net income EUR 4.96B and gross margin 57.5%, above the 55-57% guide. Q4 guided to EUR 14.2-15.2B and 2026 raised to EUR 44-45B from EUR 43-45B. CEO Christophe Fouquet said customers keep raising forecasts on AI investment, some want 2029-30 orders, and ASML is studying capacity beyond its planned 30% increase for 2028. No quarterly bookings are published any more. US-listed shares fell about 3% overnight; Micron, SanDisk and Intel fell 1-2.6%.
